findings.claim: The observed support is the full native score-node window [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score times; the curve for landmark_00_local_dx is defined only on this window and extrapolation is not allowed.

landmark_00_local_dx shows a non-monotone whole-window profile: it rises to a positive peak near the middle of the window, then falls to a negative trough, then partially recovers toward the end; the whole-window mean z is slightly negative (-0.18).

The endpoint rates of landmark_00_local_dx are strongly signed and opposite: first_rate_z is strongly negative (-17.5) while last_rate_z is strongly positive (+8.1), indicating the coordinate is changing in opposite directions at the start and end of the observed window.

The landmark_00_local_dx curve is unstable as a smooth polynomial: polynomial_accepted is false, relative_node_RMSE is 0.78, there are 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so a single global monotone trend is not supported.

hypotheses.direction: time-varying; no single monotone direction is supported
hypotheses.falsifier: If a re-read of the same curve over the full window shows no sign reversal in the node values or endpoint rates, or if the sign conflicts are resolved to a single monotone trend, the time-varying contrast claim fails.
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate exhibits a time-varying contrast over the observed window: an early-to-middle positive excursion followed by a mid-to-late negative excursion, with opposite endpoint rates. This motivates testing whether guidance dose should differ across the window rather than being uniform.

hypotheses.direction: unchanged/uncertain; do not assume early guidance is harmful or beneficial
hypotheses.falsifier: If independently stable per-batch profiles show a consistent knot location, the phase-knot hypothesis would be supported rather than merely assumed.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx curve stability metrics (polynomial_accepted, sign_changes, strong_sign_conflicts)
hypotheses.statement: Because the curve is non-polynomial and has many sign changes and strong sign conflicts across batches, any temporal dose recipe keyed to a fixed normalized phase (e.g., early/middle/late knots) is a hypothesis about timing, not a discovered stage boundary.

limitations: Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; other landmark coordinates and soft_mass features were not queried, so cross-feature consistency is unobserved.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves are accessible.
Descendant final quality and decoded final affinity are not observed in this role input, so selection preference cannot be equated with measured final benefit.
The curve is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world A; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
Unqueried evidence is not unavailable evidence; additional features may contradict or refine these findings.
